statement: deterministic addressing achieved perfect internal coverage and failed to transfer, because its language-to-address interface was coupled to the grammar of the corpus it was written against. Five of six supposedly general constructions match nothing on 1200 external questions, and the apparent 0.446 coverage comes from a catch-all preposition matcher yielding service.them, service.years and service.tomorrow

the_model_now_has_an_evidenced_place.now_supported: literal and grammatical rules do not transfer across corpora. That is the first failure mode in this project that a model is a plausible answer to, and it is narrow: resolving language to an address where deterministic rules abstain
previously_refuted: a model is needed for property resolution — canonicalisation sufficed
a model is needed for entity resolution — canonicalisation sufficed internally
the_model_now_has_an_evidenced_place.question: can a small model used only for unresolved language-to-address mapping generalise while the memory structure stays deterministic?
the_model_now_has_an_evidenced_place.shape: deterministic exact evidence first — identifiers, aliases, numbers, paths, schema matches. On abstention, a small model chooses from controlled candidate sets. A deterministic validator accepts or abstains. The model resolves language; it does not manage memory

what_failed: the first bridge only: natural language to entity, property and scope
